identity.name: Holy Roman Empire
alt_names: Holy Roman Empire of the Middle Ages

land.text: the whole realm of Otto I, the German kingdom and, from late 961, Italy

predecessors.note: Not a conquest: the Kingdom of Germany dossier (eu-08-a) ends in February 962 with the imperial coronation and names this dossier as its successor.

land.text: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Italy shape of 962-969, 623 of whose 657 cells lie inside this dossier's 962 shape

predecessors.note: Per the Kingdom of Germany dossier (eu-08-a) Italy was Berengar's vassal kingdom 952-961 and came to Otto in late 961; Cliopatria draws it twice for 962-969.

land.text: the Empire's directly held lands from 1260, Cliopatria's second row for the same empire

successors.note: Same state, not a new one: the two rows share Wikidata Q12548 and the Holy Roman Empire page runs to 'Dissolution: 6 August 1806'. The split at 1260 is Cliopatria's; the group eu-09 writes the second row. The colour agent should give both the same colour.

capitals.name: Itinerant court (Frankfurt and Aachen named for elections and coronations)
capitals.note: No fixed capital: 'kings and emperors continued to travel around the empire well into modern times, using their temporary residences (Kaiserpfalz) as transit stations for their itinerant courts'; 'The emperors continued to travel to their elections and coronations at Frankfurt and Aachen'. Frankfurt is plotted as in the Kingdom of Germany dossier; imperial coronations took place in Rome (962, 1014, 1027, 1155, 1220).

keyframe_review.note: 737,034 km2 for 962-969: Germany, Austria and Italy down to Spoleto. It contains 623 of the 657 cells of Cliopatria's Kingdom of Italy shape of 962-969, so the Italian half is drawn twice (Kingdom of Italy row and this one) until 970. Central Italy (the Duchy of Spoleto, 88 cells) is inside; the Otto I page says the Diploma Ottonianum of 962 expanded the Pope's domain by 'the Exarchate of Ravenna and the Duchy of Spoleto', which the shape does not follow. Unverified: page budget.

724,772 km2 for 970-979: Cliopatria passes the Spoleto lands (88 cells) to the Duchy of Benevento's shape and adds Corsica. The Otto I page has Pandolf Ironhead of Benevento accept Otto as overlord from February 967 and the Byzantines accept Otto's dominion over Capua, Benevento and Salerno in 972, which is consistent with a vassal Benevento holding Spoleto; the Corsican cells are not on any page opened. Unverified: page budget.

correction.text: unchanged shape; it holds 980-982 and the Slav marches east of the Elbe are lost in 983 ('The Northern March and the Billung March were lost')

keyframe_review.note: 724,602 km2 for 980-989. The Great Slav Rising page dates the loss of Havelberg and Brandenburg to 29 June 983 and the Northern and Billung Marches to the revolt of 983; Cliopatria's shape keeps them until 989 and drops them in 990. The shape holds for 980-982 only; 983-989 use the new keyframe holy-roman-empire_983.

correction.text: the Empire behind the Elbe after the revolt of 983: Cliopatria's 990 shape without the Spoleto cells that stay with Benevento until 989

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 983-989: the 990 shape less the Spoleto cells that Cliopatria still gives to Benevento until 989 (they return in 990). Brandenburg and the Havelland to the Lutici, the Billung March and the Obotrite coast to the Obotrites; 'A hastily assembled Saxon army was only able to retain the Slavs behind the Elbe'; the Lusatian, Zeitz, Merseburg and Meissen marches 'did not take part in the uprising'.

701,841 km2 for 990-1002: the Empire behind the Elbe line after the 983 revolt; 'The immediate consequences of the uprising were an almost complete stop on further German eastward expansion for the next 200 years.' The central Italian cells return in 990 (no page).

646,697 km2 for 1003-1009: Bolesław I of Poland holds Meissen and Lusatia ('occupied the March of Meissen and the March of Lusatia', 1002) and Bohemia ('invaded Bohemia in 1003 and conquered the duchy'). Cliopatria's shape also drops 36 Austrian cells to its Poland shape, which no page opened supports. Unverified: page budget.

729,594 km2 for 1010-1017: Bohemia, Meissen and Lusatia are back (the Holy Roman Empire page lists the Duchy of Bohemia in the Empire 'from 1002'), and the Genoa and Pisa cells leave. Henry II's war with Poland ran 1004-1018 (Peace of Bautzen 30 January 1018); Bohemia, Meissen and Lusatia are the contested zone, blended 1004-1018 by the ledger. Unverified: page budget.

correction.text: unchanged shape; Lusatia and Meissen become a nominal fief held by Bolesław of Poland (vassal tint) 1018-1033

keyframe_review.note: 729,525 km2 for 1018-1027, shape unchanged; status changes. The Henry II page: 'Poland kept Lusatia and Meissen, which Bolesław held on purely nominal terms of vassalage.' Lusatia and Meissen are drawn as the lighter vassal tint from 1018 to 1033 (ledger vassal_start/vassal_end), not as direct Imperial land.

762,559 km2 for 1028-1033: Moravia, the cells north of it and 19 Lower Austrian cells are added. Conrad II page: Oldřich was 'reconquer[ing] Moravia by 1029'; Cliopatria draws the 1028 shape one year before the page's 'by 1029', within precision.

894,318 km2 for 1034-1039: the Kingdom of Burgundy (Arles) is added, 480 of the 543 new cells, as 'On 1 August 1034, Conrad officially incorporated Burgundy into the Holy Roman Empire' (infobox of the Holy Roman Empire page: 2 February 1033). The other 62 cells are the Lusatian lands the Treaty of Merseburg returned in 1033. The kingdom is a component with its own autonomy, which the Kingdom of Arles dossier (eu-08-a) records.
894,478 km2 for 1040-1065: no border change in Cliopatria (+2 cells). No page opened covers Henry III (1039-1056). Unverified: page budget.
894,501 km2 for 1066-1093: no change (Henry IV's reign 1056-1106; the Holy Roman Empire page gives 'the famous Walk to Canossa in 1077'), no territorial event on the page. Unverified: page budget.
883,261 km2 for 1094-1098: Corsica (34 cells) passes to the Republic of Pisa's shape. No page opened mentions Corsica. Unverified: page budget.
883,283 km2 for 1099-1125: no change. The Holy Roman Empire page dates the Concordat of Worms to 1122 and the end of the Salian line to 1125. Unverified: page budget.
880,445 km2 for 1126-1138: 12 cells in the Lubusz land leave for the Kingdom of Poland's shape. No page opened explains it. Unverified: page budget.

891,038 km2 for 1139-1146; the infobox of the Holy Roman Empire page gives 'in year 1150: 1,100,000 km2 (420,000 sq mi)' against 874,000 km2 for the 1147 shape (ratio 0.79): within a factor of two; the page does not say what the infobox counts. Corsica (34 cells) is back in the shape, 34 cells shared with the Republic of Pisa's shape, which Cliopatria draws on top. Unverified: page budget.

873,727 km2 for 1147-1151: eastern Holstein is added (21 cells) after the Wendish Crusade of 1147, and the Abruzzo (40 cells) and Corsica (34) leave; infobox 1,100,000 km2 for 1150 (ratio 0.79). The Abruzzo and Corsica changes are on no page opened.

correction.text: unchanged shape; it holds 1152-1156, Brandenburg comes back in 1157

keyframe_review.note: 873,954 km2 for 1152-1168. The Great Slav Rising page dates the Margraviate of Brandenburg to 1157 ('the establishment of the Margraviate of Brandenburg under the Ascanian prince Albert the Bear in 1157, the settlements east of the Elbe were resumed') and Cliopatria adds Brandenburg only in 1169. The shape holds 1152-1156; 1157-1163 use the new keyframe holy-roman-empire_1157.

correction.text: the 1152 shape plus the March of Brandenburg (1157)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1157-1163: the 1152 shape plus Brandenburg, the Havelland, the Altmark and Berlin (98 cells) won by Albert the Bear in 1157.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1169 shape, taken from 1164; its Mecklenburg-Vorpommern coast is a vassal land of Henry the Lion

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1164-1168: Cliopatria's 1169 shape (913,708 km2, the largest of the row), whose Mecklenburg-Vorpommern coast is, by the Duchy of Pomerania page, a vassal land from 1164: 'the Pomeranian dukes became vassals of Henry the Lion, of Saxony' after the Battle of Verchen.

correction.text: unchanged shape; the Mecklenburg-Vorpommern coast is drawn as a vassal tint

keyframe_review.note: 913,708 km2 for 1169-1176: shape unchanged; the Mecklenburg-Vorpommern coast (79 cells) is a vassal land, not direct: 'the Pomeranian dukes became vassals of Henry the Lion, of Saxony' (1164), 'In 1181 the dukes took their duchy as a fief from the Holy Roman Emperor Barbarossa'. The Henry the Lion page gives only 'from Westphalia to Pomerania' for his realm and nothing on Mecklenburg.

correction.text: the 1177 shape plus the Baltic coast of the 1169 shape (Pomerania and the Mecklenburg coast), vassal land until 1184

keyframe_review.note: 889,637 km2 for 1177-1187: Cliopatria drops the Baltic coast (107 cells, 105 of them in its Denmark shape) in 1177, but the Duchy of Pomerania page makes Bogislaw I a vassal of the Emperor from 1181 and a Danish vassal only from 1185 ('In 1184 and 1185, three campaigns of the Danes'). The coast stays in, as a vassal, until 1184; the 1177 shape holds 1177-1184 with it, and the new keyframe holy-roman-empire_1185 holds 1185-1187.
New keyframe for 1185-1187: Cliopatria's 1177 shape as drawn, once Pomerania is a Danish vassal.

correction.text: unchanged shape; it holds 1188-1197, Bohemia becomes a kingdom in 1198

keyframe_review.note: 879,438 km2 for 1188-1201: the shape loses 46 cells of south-eastern France in 1188 (no page, unverified) and still includes Bohemia and Moravia. The Holy Roman Empire page: Bohemia was 'raised to a kingdom in 1198'. The shape holds 1188-1197; 1198-1201 use the new keyframe holy-roman-empire_1198.

correction.text: the 1188 shape without Bohemia and Moravia, now a kingdom and vassal

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1198-1201: the 1188 shape less the Kingdom of Bohemia's shape of 1202 (292 cells), which the Holy Roman Empire page makes a kingdom in 1198 ('In 1212, King Ottokar I (bearing the title "king" since 1198) extracted a Golden Bull of Sicily'). Holstein is still inside until the Danish conquest of 1203.

795,670 km2 for 1202-1205: Bohemia and Moravia are out (kingdom and vassal), and Holstein, Lübeck and Hamburg are out. The Valdemar II page: 'In 1203 Valdemar invaded and conquered Lybeck and Holstein' (the lead gives 1207), a year after the shape.
795,601 km2 for 1206-1215: no change. Philip of Swabia is murdered in 1208 and Otto IV prevails (Holy Roman Empire page). No territorial event. Unverified: page budget.

correction.text: unchanged shape; it holds 1216-1226, the southern Baltic shore returns after Bornhöved in 1227

keyframe_review.note: 795,902 km2 for 1216-1235. The Valdemar II page: Denmark loses its north German territories after the capture of Valdemar in 1223, the defeat at Mölln in 1225 and the Battle of Bornhöved on 22 July 1227; Cliopatria returns them to the Empire only in 1236. The shape holds 1216-1226; 1227-1235 use the new keyframe holy-roman-empire_1227.

New keyframe for 1227-1235: the 1236 shape (Holstein, Mecklenburg, Pomerania and the Baltic coast back in the Empire's reach). 'A series of Danish defeats culminating in the Battle of Bornhöved on 22 July 1227 cemented the loss of Denmark's north German territories'; the Duchy of Pomerania page: 'Denmark lost all her territories on the southern Baltic shore, including Pomerania.' Pomerania is a vassal land.

correction.text: unchanged shape; Pomerania is drawn as a vassal tint (the duchy under Brandenburg's overlordship)

keyframe_review.note: 858,754 km2 for 1236-1249: shape unchanged; Pomerania is a vassal land. 'Wartislaw had to accept Brandenburg's overlordship in the 1236 Treaty of Kremmen' and had to hand most of his duchy, including the Burg Stargard Land, over to Brandenburg. Pomeranian Voivodeship cells (28) lie east of Pomerania proper (Pomerelia); the Duchy of Pomerania page does not place them in the Empire's reach. Unverified: page budget.

858,863 km2 for 1250-1259: no change. Frederick II died on 13 December 1250 ('26 December 1194 - 13 December 1250'); Conrad IV died in 1254, 'followed by the Interregnum'. The row ends in 1259; the Empire continues under 'Holy Roman Empire Minor States' from 1260.

correction.text: use Cliopatria's 'Holy Roman Empire Minor States' shape of 1619 for the Empire in 1619-1621; the stray Bohemian-Crown fragment is not the Empire

keyframe_review.note: 145,397 km2 for 1619-1621, bbox 7.0-19.2 E, 48.6-52.3 N: 604 cells: 317 in Czechia (230 of them Bohemia, 63 Moravia), 173 in Poland (164 Silesia) and 111 in Germany (Lusatia and Saxony). That is the Lands of the Bohemian Crown, not the Empire, which existed until 'Dissolution: 6 August 1806' (Holy Roman Empire page). The Empire in 1619-1621 is the row 'Holy Roman Empire Minor States' (1,240 cells in 1619, eu-09). The shape belongs to the Bohemian Revolt, a Kingdom of Bohemia / Habsburg question outside this batch's scope (to 1250); no page on it was opened.

region.text: the realm of Otto I at his coronation: the German kingdom and the Italian kingdom (Cliopatria's 962 shape)

ledger.note: 962: Otto I is crowned emperor in Rome and the Empire begins. Otto I page: 'he was crowned Emperor by Pope John XII at Old St. Peter's Basilica', three days after reaching Rome on 31 January; the Holy Roman Empire page infobox gives 'Otto I crowned Emperor: 2 February 962' and the text 'In 962, Otto was crowned emperor by Pope John XII.' The pages name the coronation, not a boundary: the region is Cliopatria's 962 shape (Germany, Austria and northern and central Italy). The same infobox starts the Empire with 'Charlemagne crowned Emperor: 25 December 800'; this dossier follows Cliopatria and the Kingdom of Germany dossier (eu-08-a), whose successor it is, and starts at 962.

region.text: the central Italian cells (Umbria, Marche, Abruzzo: the Duchy of Spoleto) that Cliopatria's 962-969 shape has and its 970 shape lacks

ledger.note: 970: Cliopatria hands the March of Spoleto and Camerino lands to the Duchy of Benevento. The Otto I page says only 'Since February 967, the Prince of Benevento, Lombard Pandolf Ironhead, had accepted Otto as his overlord' and, for 962, that the Diploma Ottonianum expanded the Pope's domain by 'several territories, including the Exarchate of Ravenna and the Duchy of Spoleto'; it does not say who held Spoleto in 970. The 88 cells (Perugia, L'Aquila, Macerata, Rieti, Teramo, Chieti, Ascoli Piceno, Terni) are in the Kingdom of Italy's 962-969 shape and in Benevento's 970-989 shape; the date is Cliopatria's.

region.text: Corsica

ledger.note: 970: Cliopatria's shape adds Corsica (33 cells, 34 with the neighbouring islets) to the Empire; the Otto I page has 'Corsica or Sardinia: not on page'. Until 969 the island is in the Kingdom of Italy row; it passes to Pisa in 1094 and back in 1139. Unverified: page budget.

region.text: the Billung March and the Obotrite coast: Oldenburg in Holstein, Mecklenburg, Vorpommern

ledger.note: 983: the Obotrites join the revolt and the Billung March goes. 'the Obotrites joined the Lutici, devastated a St Lawrence monastery in Kalbe, the bishopric of Oldenburg and even assaulted Hamburg'; 'The Northern March and the Billung March were lost.' The page does not name Mecklenburg or Holstein as 983 losses; the region is the rest of Cliopatria's 980-to-990 loss (Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and eastern Holstein).

region.text: the Northern March east of the Elbe: Havelberg, Brandenburg and the Havelland, lost to the Lutici

ledger.note: 983: the Slav revolt takes the Elbe-Oder marches. 'the bishops' seat of Havelberg on 29 June 983 was occupied and plundered', 'followed by Brandenburg three days later'; 'The Northern March and the Billung March were lost.' 'A hastily assembled Saxon army was only able to retain the Slavs behind the Elbe.' This event is the Lutici share (Brandenburg, the Havelland, the Altmark and Berlin cells of Cliopatria's 980 shape that its 990 shape lacks).

region.text: the marches east of the Elbe lost in 983

ledger.note: 985: 'From 985, several princes of the Empire carried out annual campaigns' to win back the lands east of the Elbe; the Elbe line holds and the Slav lands stay in dispute until the alliance of 1003.

region.text: the same 88 central Italian cells as the 970 loss

ledger.note: 990: Cliopatria returns the central Italian cells (Spoleto, Camerino, Marche, Abruzzo) from the Duchy of Benevento's shape to the Empire. No page opened dates or explains the return; the Otto I page has Pandolf of Benevento accept Otto as overlord from February 967 and the Byzantines accept Otto's dominion over Capua, Benevento and Salerno in 972, and nothing later.

region.text: the March of Meissen and the March of Lusatia, with the adjoining marches Cliopatria's 1003 shape drops

ledger.note: 1002: Bolesław I of Poland takes Meissen and Lusatia. 'Bolesław I occupied the March of Meissen and the March of Lusatia', 'occupying important German territories west of the Oder River' (Henry II page, under 1002). Cliopatria's shape drops them in 1003. The Great Slav Rising page says the Lusatian, Zeitz, Merseburg and Meissen marches 'did not take part in the uprising' of 983.

region.text: Pavia, where Arduin proclaimed himself King of Italy

ledger.note: 1002: Arduin of Ivrea 'proclaimed himself King of Italy at Pavia soon after the Emperor's death' (Henry II page), setting up a rival kingdom in Lombardy against the German king.

region.text: Cliopatria's Austrian and Bavarian cells that pass to its Poland shape in 1003

ledger.note: 1003: Cliopatria's 1003 shape also drops 36 cells in Lower and Upper Austria (and 6 in Bavaria) to its Kingdom of Poland shape. The Henry II page, the Great Slav Rising page and the Holy Roman Empire page say nothing about Austria in 1003; page silent. Unverified: page budget.

region.text: the marches east of the Elbe lost in 983

ledger.note: 1003: the Empire changes course in the east: 'In 1003 King Henry II of Germany tried a different approach: he allied himself with the Lutici and waged war against Bolesław.' The annual campaigns against the Slavs of 985-1003 end in an alliance (Henry II page: 'formed an alliance with the pagan Slavic Lutici tribe').

region.text: Bohemia, the March of Meissen and the March of Lusatia, held by Bolesław I from 1002-1003

ledger.note: 1004: Henry II opens his war with Poland. The campaign 'lasted until 1018, encompassing three wars and several smaller campaigns'; Henry 'joined Duke Jaromír of Bohemia in his struggle against the Poles'. Bolesław had 'invaded Bohemia in 1003 and conquered the duchy without any serious opposition'. Zone: Bohemia, Meissen and Lusatia (the lands Cliopatria's shape regains by 1010).

region.text: Pavia, where Henry was crowned

ledger.note: 1004: Henry II is crowned King of Italy at Pavia on 14 May 1004 (Arnulf II; the page's lead and infobox give 15 May). The page names no ground Arduin kept after that and has him 'resign his margraviate and die on 14 December 1015', so the contest is closed at the coronation.

region.text: Bohemia, the March of Meissen and the March of Lusatia

ledger.note: 1010: Cliopatria's shape takes back Bohemia, Meissen and Lusatia (and 17 Austrian cells) from its Poland shape. Page silent on the date of the recovery: the Henry II page dates only the start of the war (1004), the Merseburg treaty ('requiring in part that Bolesław I recognize Henry II as his overlord', 1013) and the Peace of Bautzen (1018). The Holy Roman Empire page lists Bohemia among the Empire's lands 'from 1002 as the Duchy of Bohemia'.

region.text: the Tuscan coastal cells that Cliopatria's 1010 shape lacks

ledger.note: 1010: the Republic of Pisa begins in Cliopatria and takes 12 cells of the Empire's Tuscan coast. No page opened dates the commune's independence; page silent. Unverified: page budget.

region.text: the Ligurian coastal cells that Cliopatria's 1010 shape lacks

ledger.note: 1010: the Republic of Genoa begins in Cliopatria and takes the Empire's Ligurian coast (18 cells, 16 of them in Genoa's 1010 shape). No page opened dates the commune's independence; page silent. Unverified: page budget.

region.text: Meissen and Lusatia as Bolesław's nominal fief

ledger.note: 1018: Lusatia and Meissen stay with Poland as a nominal fief: 'Poland kept Lusatia and Meissen, which Bolesław held on purely nominal terms of vassalage.' Cliopatria keeps both inside the Empire's shape throughout; they are drawn as the lighter vassal tint until 1033. The Conrad II page speaks of Mieszko II invading 'Lusatia' in 1028 as if it were Imperial, so the two pages are not fully consistent.

region.text: Bohemia, the March of Meissen and the March of Lusatia

ledger.note: 1018: the war with Poland ends. 'On 30 January, Henry and Bolesław signed a fourth peace treaty, known as the Peace of Bautzen.' (Henry II page.) Treaty of Merseburg of 1013: 'requiring in part that Bolesław I recognize Henry II as his overlord'.

1024: the Salian dynasty succeeds the Ottonians. 'Henry II died in 1024 and Conrad II, first of the Salian dynasty, was elected king only after some debate among dukes and nobles.' (Conrad II page: elected 4 September 1024, crowned at Mainz 8 September.) Same state, same colour.

region.text: Lusatia and Meissen

ledger.note: 1028: war with Poland resumes: Mieszko II 'took the initiative and invaded Lusatia'. Zone: Lusatia and Meissen.

region.text: Moravia and the cells north and south of it that Cliopatria's 1028 shape adds

ledger.note: 1029: Moravia returns from Poland to Bohemia, then an Imperial duchy. Conrad II page: Oldřich was 'reconquer[ing] Moravia by 1029' after going on the offensive against Poland. Cliopatria's shape carries Moravia, Silesian and Lower Austrian cells from 1028; the year of the page ('by 1029') leaves 1028 open. 'Silesia' here is Cliopatria's reading of the shape; the page names only Moravia.

region.text: Lusatia and Meissen

ledger.note: 1031: Mieszko II surrenders: 'Mieszko surrendered to Conrad in the fall, and the Treaty of Merseburg required the return of Meissen and Lusatia.' (The page dates the assembly that issued the treaty to July 1033.)

region.text: the western territory of Rudolph III's kingdom held by Odo II of Blois

ledger.note: 1033: Conrad II claims the Kingdom of Burgundy against Odo II of Blois. 'Rudolph died on 6 September 1032'; 'Count Odo II of Blois had already invaded the kingdom' and held much of its western territory; on 2 February 1033 Conrad 'arrived at Vaud, where he held an assembly at the Abbey of Payerne' and was crowned king of Burgundy there, but 'had to withdraw to Zürich in March' after little progress against Odo.

region.text: Lusatia and Meissen

ledger.note: 1033: Lusatia and Meissen come back: the Treaty of Merseburg 'required the return of Meissen and Lusatia', issued at the assembly of July 1033 that 'restored Mieszko to the Polish throne'.

region.text: the Lusatian cells that Cliopatria's 1034 shape adds, returned by the Treaty of Merseburg

ledger.note: 1033: the rest of Lusatia returns to the Empire's shape under the same treaty; Cliopatria adds them in 1034 (62 cells, taken from its Poland shape). The page says 'Meissen and Lusatia'; the cells are Cliopatria's.

region.text: the western territory of Rudolph III's kingdom held by Odo II of Blois

ledger.note: 1034: Odo's hold on western Burgundy ends no later than the incorporation of the kingdom. The Conrad II page does not say how or when Odo's districts were recovered; closed at the incorporation date. Page silent.

region.text: the Kingdom of Burgundy: Burgundy, Provence, the Dauphiné and Savoy, Franche-Comté and western Switzerland

ledger.note: 1034: Conrad II incorporates the Kingdom of Burgundy (Arles). 'On 1 August 1034, Conrad officially incorporated Burgundy into the Holy Roman Empire' at Geneva; Burgundian and Provençal nobles 'paid homage to Conrad in Zürich in 1034'. The Holy Roman Empire page infobox dates the incorporation 2 February 1033 and the list 'from 1032 to 1378'. The kingdom kept its own autonomy and is a component of the Empire; Cliopatria's Arles shape of 1034-1384 is a mis-placed strip (see the Kingdom of Arles dossier, eu-08-a).

region.text: Corsica

ledger.note: 1094: Corsica passes from the Empire's shape to the Republic of Pisa's shape in Cliopatria. No page opened mentions Corsica; page silent. Unverified: page budget.

1125: the Salian line ends and the crown passes to Lothair III. 'When the Salian dynasty ended with Henry V's death in 1125'; Henry V had 'reached an agreement with the Pope and the bishops in the 1122 Concordat of Worms'. The page gives Lothair's death as 1137. Same state, same colour.

region.text: the Lubusz cells that Cliopatria's 1126 shape lacks

ledger.note: 1126: 12 cells in the Lubusz land east of the Oder pass from the Empire's shape to Cliopatria's Kingdom of Poland shape. No page opened explains it; page silent. Unverified: page budget.

1138: the Hohenstaufen succeed Lothair III. The Holy Roman Empire page gives 'When he died in 1137' (Lothair) and 'after his death in 1152, his nephew Frederick Barbarossa succeeded him' (Conrad III) but not Conrad's election; the Henry the Lion page has Conrad III 'handing Saxony to Albert the Bear' in 1138. Year bridged from those two sentences. Same state, same colour.

region.text: Corsica, with four eastern cells

ledger.note: 1139: Cliopatria's shape takes Corsica back from the Republic of Pisa's shape (and four cells in the east from its Poland shape). No page opened mentions it; page silent. Unverified: page budget.

region.text: eastern Holstein, the Obotrite coast opened by the Wendish Crusade

ledger.note: 1147: the Wendish Crusade reaches the Slav coast of Holstein. Great Slav Rising page: 'Only in the 12th century after the Wendish Crusade of 1147 and the establishment of the Margraviate of Brandenburg under the Ascanian prince Albert the Bear in 1157, the settlements east of the Elbe were resumed.' Henry the Lion page: 'A participant in the 1147 Wendish Crusade.' The 21 cells are eastern Holstein (Wagria); the page names neither Wagria nor Holstein.

region.text: the Abruzzo cells that Cliopatria's 1147 shape lacks

ledger.note: 1147: Cliopatria's shape drops the Abruzzo cells (L'Aquila, Teramo, Chieti, Rieti, Pescara: 40 cells) to the Kingdom of Sicily's shape. No page opened dates the change; page silent. Unverified: page budget.

region.text: Corsica

ledger.note: 1147: Corsica (34 cells) leaves the Empire's shape for the Republic of Pisa's. No page opened mentions Corsica; page silent. Unverified: page budget.

region.text: the Havelland and Brandenburg, lost to the Slavs in 983

ledger.note: 1157: Albert the Bear's Margraviate of Brandenburg takes the Havelland back. 'the establishment of the Margraviate of Brandenburg under the Ascanian prince Albert the Bear in 1157, the settlements east of the Elbe were resumed.' Cliopatria's shape carries the Brandenburg, Berlin and Altmark cells from 1169; the page gives 1157.

region.text: Pomerania and the Mecklenburg coast, vassal of Henry the Lion

ledger.note: 1164: the Pomeranian dukes become vassals within the Empire. Duchy of Pomerania page: 'the Pomeranian dukes became vassals of Henry the Lion, of Saxony' after the Battle of Verchen. The page speaks of the Pomeranian dukes; Cliopatria's 1169 shape draws the whole Mecklenburg-Vorpommern coast with them (79 cells), and the page is silent on Mecklenburg's status.

region.text: Pomerania and the Mecklenburg coast

ledger.note: 1185: Pomerania passes to Denmark. 'In 1184 and 1185, three campaigns of the Danes resulted in making Bogislaw I, Duke of Pomerania a Danish vassal' (infobox: Danish vassal 1185-1227). Before that, 'In 1181 the dukes took their duchy as a fief from the Holy Roman Emperor Barbarossa'. Cliopatria moves the Baltic coast to its Denmark shape already in 1177.

region.text: the Baltic coast that Cliopatria's 1177 shape lacks

ledger.note: 1185: the Baltic coast between the Elbe and the Oder leaves the Empire's reach for Denmark. Cliopatria drops the 107 cells in 1177 (75 in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, 30 in Brandenburg) and its Denmark shape holds 105 of them; the page dates the Danish overlordship of Pomerania to 1184-1185 and says nothing of the Brandenburg cells.

region.text: the Lyonnais, Forez, Bresse and Mâconnais cells that Cliopatria's 1188 shape lacks

ledger.note: 1188: Cliopatria's shape loses 46 cells of south-eastern France (Loire, Rhône, Ain, Saône-et-Loire) to its Kingdom of France shape (32) and its Arles strip (14). No page opened dates a change on the Burgundian frontier in 1177-1188; page silent. Unverified: page budget.

region.text: Bohemia and Moravia, the Přemyslid kingdom (Cliopatria's Kingdom of Bohemia shape of 1202)

ledger.note: 1198: Bohemia becomes a kingdom within the Empire. 'Kingdom of Bohemia (from 1002 as the Duchy of Bohemia and raised to a kingdom in 1198)'; 'In 1212, King Ottokar I (bearing the title "king" since 1198) extracted a Golden Bull of Sicily' confirming the royal title. Cliopatria starts its Kingdom of Bohemia row, and its vassalage of Bohemia to the Empire, in 1202; the page gives 1198.

region.text: Holstein, Lübeck and Hamburg

ledger.note: 1201: Valdemar of Denmark takes the field against Holstein: 'He defeated and captured the count at the Battle of Stellau in 1201' (Count Adolf III of Holstein).

region.text: Holstein and Lübeck

ledger.note: 1203: Holstein and Lübeck fall to Denmark. 'In 1203 Valdemar invaded and conquered Lybeck and Holstein, adding them to the territories controlled by Denmark' (the lead gives 1207). Cliopatria's shape drops them in 1202. Confidence 2 (reviewer eu-08-b): the page dates the conquest 1203 in the body and 1207 in the lead.

region.text: Holstein and Lübeck

ledger.note: 1203: the contest over Holstein is settled by the Danish conquest; Danish rule holds until 1223-1227.

region.text: Holstein, Mecklenburg, Pomerania and the Baltic coast held by Denmark

ledger.note: 1223: the Danes lose their north German holdings. 'In 1223, King Valdemar and his eldest son, prince Valdemar, were abducted by Count Henry I of Schwerin'; 'While Valdemar sat in prison, most of the German territories tore themselves away from Denmark'; the Danish army is beaten at Mölln in 1225.

region.text: Holstein, Mecklenburg, Pomerania and the Baltic coast held by Denmark

ledger.note: 1227: Bornhöved ends the contest. 'A series of Danish defeats culminating in the Battle of Bornhöved on 22 July 1227 cemented the loss of Denmark's north German territories.' Duchy of Pomerania page: 'Denmark lost all her territories on the southern Baltic shore, including Pomerania.'

region.text: Holstein, Mecklenburg, Pomerania and the Baltic coast

ledger.note: 1227: the southern Baltic shore comes back to the Empire's side after Bornhöved. 'Denmark lost all her territories on the southern Baltic shore, including Pomerania.' Cliopatria's Denmark shape holds 267 of these 268 cells until 1235 and gives them to the Empire in 1236. The page names Pomerania; Holstein and Mecklenburg are the Valdemar II page's 'north German territories'.

region.text: the Duchy of Pomerania

ledger.note: 1227: Pomerania is again under the Empire's suzerainty after the Danes leave: 'From the late 12th century, the Duchy of Pomerania was under the suzerainty of the Holy Roman Empire' (Holy Roman Empire page). The Pomerania page: Denmark 'took Wolgast and Demmin in 1235, but was driven out the same year'. Drawn as a vassal tint.

region.text: the Burg Stargard Land, given to Brandenburg by the Treaty of Kremmen

ledger.note: 1236: Brandenburg takes the Stargard Land from Pomerania. 'Wartislaw had to accept Brandenburg's overlordship in the 1236 Treaty of Kremmen' and had to hand most of his duchy, including the Burg Stargard Land, over to Brandenburg; Brandenburg is a march of the Empire. Cliopatria adds the whole Baltic coast to the Empire's shape in 1236.

1254: the Hohenstaufen line ends. 'After the death of Frederick II in 1250, Conrad IV, Frederick's son (died 1254)'; 'Conrad's death was followed by the Interregnum'; 'After 1257, the crown was contested between Richard of Cornwall ... and Alfonso X of Castile'. Same state, same colour.

region.text: Bohemia and Moravia

ledger.note: 1259: the Kingdom of Bohemia's vassalage ends in the dossier, not in history: Cliopatria's relation row runs 1202-1259 and its next Bohemian vassalage starts 1314; no page opened ends it.

region.text: the Duchy of Pomerania

ledger.note: 1259: the Pomeranian vassalage ends in the dossier at the row boundary, not in history; the Duchy of Pomerania page has the Treaty of Landin of 1250 restoring Barnim I's rule over Pomerania, and no end of the Empire's suzerainty.

region.text: the Empire's last shape in this row (1250-1259), continued by Cliopatria's 'Holy Roman Empire Minor States' from 1260

ledger.note: 1259: the Cliopatria row of the directly held Empire ends; the same Empire continues in the row 'Holy Roman Empire Minor States' from 1260 (shared Wikidata Q12548; the Holy Roman Empire page: 'Dissolution: 6 August 1806'). Not a collapse: a row boundary during the Interregnum.

wars.name: Great Slav Rising

zones.text: the Billung March and the Obotrite coast

wars.outcome: Slav victory: Havelberg (29 June 983) and Brandenburg (three days later) taken, the Northern and Billung Marches lost, the Elbe line held; annual Imperial campaigns from 985; Henry II allies with the Lutici in 1003.
wars.note: The page: 'The immediate consequences of the uprising were an almost complete stop on further German eastward expansion for the next 200 years.'

wars.name: Otto I's conflict with the Byzantine Empire over southern Italy
wars.outcome: Settled in 972: 'the Byzantine Empire accepted Otto's dominion over the principalities of Capua, Benevento and Salerno' and Otto 'retreated from the Byzantine possessions in Apulia and Calabria'.
wars.note: From February 967 Pandolf Ironhead of Benevento accepted Otto as overlord, which 'caused conflict with the Byzantine Empire'. The campaigns themselves are 'not on page'; no zone is drawn because the Empire's shape never reaches south of Spoleto.

wars.name: Henry II's wars against Boleslaw I of Poland

zones.text: Bohemia, the March of Meissen and the March of Lusatia

wars.outcome: Peace of Bautzen, 30 January 1018 (the fourth treaty after Merseburg 1013): Poland kept Lusatia and Meissen on nominal terms of vassalage; Bohemia stayed with the Empire.
wars.note: Bolesław occupied Meissen and Lusatia (1002) and Bohemia (1003); Henry II allied with the Lutici in 1003; three wars and several smaller campaigns 1004-1018.

wars.name: Arduin of Ivrea's rebellion
wars.outcome: Henry II crowned King of Italy at Pavia on 14 May 1004; Arduin resigned his margraviate and died on 14 December 1015.

wars.name: Conrad II's war against Poland
wars.outcome: Mieszko II invaded Lusatia in 1028 and surrendered in the fall of 1031; the Treaty of Merseburg required the return of Meissen and Lusatia and was issued at the July 1033 assembly that restored Mieszko.

wars.name: Conrad II's war against Hungary
wars.outcome: Conrad's invasion of 1030 failed in the face of Hungarian scorched earth; in 1031 'Henry gave Hungarian nobles titles to eastern Bavarian lands between the Lajta and Fischa rivers'.
wars.note: No zone: the page does not locate the lands in the gazetteer's terms and Cliopatria's shape changes nothing here.

wars.name: Succession to the Kingdom of Burgundy

zones.text: the western territory held by Odo II of Blois

wars.outcome: Conrad crowned king of Burgundy at Payerne on 2 February 1033, withdrawing to Zürich in March; 'On 1 August 1034, Conrad officially incorporated Burgundy into the Holy Roman Empire' at Geneva.
wars.note: Rudolph III died on 6 September 1032 while Conrad was campaigning against Mieszko II.

wars.name: Investiture Controversy
wars.outcome: Ended by the Concordat of Worms in 1122 ('reached an agreement with the Pope and the bishops'); no land changed hands.
wars.note: The page gives only the Walk to Canossa (1077) and the Concordat (1122); the conflict began earlier, undated on the page.

wars.name: Wendish Crusade
wars.outcome: Eastern Holstein enters the Empire's shape; the Great Slav Rising page makes the Crusade of 1147 and Albert the Bear's Brandenburg (1157) the start of the resumed eastward settlement.
wars.note: Henry the Lion was 'A participant in the 1147 Wendish Crusade' (Henry the Lion page).

wars.name: Henry the Lion's campaign against the Pomeranians
wars.outcome: After the Battle of Verchen 'the Pomeranian dukes became vassals of Henry the Lion, of Saxony'; in 1181 the dukes took their duchy as a fief from Barbarossa.

wars.name: Danish conquest of Holstein and Lübeck
wars.outcome: Valdemar II took Count Adolf III of Holstein at Stellau (1201), conquered Lübeck and Holstein (1203), Stade (1214) and Hamburg (1216); captured in 1223, he lost the German lands, was beaten at Mölln (1225) and at Bornhöved (22 July 1227).
wars.note: The lead of the page dates the Holstein conquest 1207; the body 1203.

wars.name: War with the Lombard League
wars.outcome: Frederick II 'won a great victory over the Lombard League at the Battle of Cortenuova' in November 1237; no border change is drawn.
wars.note: The page dates the peace of San Germano (with the Pope) to July 1230; the start of the Lombard war is not given.

wars.name: Conflict between Frederick II and the Papacy
wars.outcome: Frederick excommunicated on 29 September 1227 and again in 1239, deposed at Lyon in 1245; he died on 13 December 1250.
wars.note: No land changed hands in Cliopatria's shapes.

certainty.note: Frontiers are the marches, duchies and bishoprics of a feudal empire: the eastern frontier moves with campaigns (983, 1002-1018, 1157, 1227), Italian and Burgundian lands are held with varying autonomy, and no treaty in the period fixes a surveyed line. The Peace of Bautzen (1018) and the Treaty of Merseburg (1033) name marches (Lusatia, Meissen), not lines.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 by the Phase B agent for batch eu-08-b (one state, nine pages opened of the nine allowed for 26 shapes).

ONE STATE OR TWO. Cliopatria's 'Holy Roman Empire' (962..1259, plus a stray 1619..1621 shape) and 'Holy Roman Empire Minor States' (1260..1806) share Wikidata Q12548 and the Wikipedia article 'Holy Roman Empire'; they are one empire, split by Cliopatria at 1260 for the directly held land. eu-09 owns holy-roman-empire-minor-states and writes it separately, so this dossier lists only the Name 'Holy Roman Empire', ends at 1259 and names the second row as successor (a row boundary, not a collapse; the dissolve event is at confidence 1 and its note says so). The colour agent should treat the two as one colour (family germany); the state page should link them. The article's infobox starts the Empire at 'Charlemagne crowned Emperor: 25 December 800'; this dossier starts at 962 with Cliopatria and the Kingdom of Germany dossier (eu-08-a), whose successor it is.

THE 1619..1621 SHAPE is not the Empire: 604 cells in Bohemia, Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia (the Lands of the Bohemian Crown during the Bohemian Revolt). Marked wrong, correction: use the Minor States shape for the Empire in 1619-1621. The Kingdom of Bohemia / Habsburg groups should decide whom the fragment belongs to (the Bohemian Revolt page was not opened: outside the group's scope to 1250).

WHAT THE SHAPE IS. The leaf 'Holy Roman Empire' draws the directly held Empire: the German kingdom, Austria, the Italian kingdom north of the Papal States (Corsica in some years), Bohemia and Moravia (1010-1201), and from 1034 the Kingdom of Burgundy (Arles; 480 of its 543 new cells are the Arles shape of 936-1033). Kingdom of Germany and Kingdom of Italy are not separate shapes after 969; the Arles shell is inside this shape (eu-08-a's request: record Arles as a component: done in the 1034 gain). The Kingdom of Bohemia is a vassal 1198/1202-1259 (Cliopatria relation 1202..1259), the personal union with the Kingdom of Sicily (Cliopatria 1216..1259) is not territory and has no ledger type; both are for the state page.

SHAPE CHANGES EXPLAINED BY PAGES (9 pages): 962 coronation; 983 Slav revolt (P3); 1002-1003 Poland takes Meissen, Lusatia and Bohemia (P4); 1018 Bautzen and 1033 Merseburg (P4, P5); 1029 Moravia (P5); 1034 Burgundy (P5); 1147 Wendish Crusade, 1157 Brandenburg (P3); 1164 Verchen, 1181 and 1185 Pomerania (P8); 1198 Bohemia kingdom (P1); 1203 Holstein and Lübeck, 1223-1227 (P7); 1236 Kremmen (P8). Six new keyframes (983, 1157, 1164, 1185, 1198, 1227) correct years that Cliopatria dates late or early; eight existing shapes are adjusted for years or status (980, 1018, 1152, 1169, 1177, 1188, 1216, 1236) and the 1619 shape is wrong.

NOT SETTLED (page silent or budget spent):
- Corsica (33-34 cells) is in the shape 970-1093 and 1126-1146 and overlaps the Republic of Pisa's shape (34 cells) in 1139-1146; no page opened mentions it. Probably a nominal Italian-kingdom claim; the Pisa and Genoa dossiers (eu-13) should decide. Events at confidence 1.
- The central-Italian cells (Duchy of Spoleto, Camerino, Marche, Abruzzo: 88 cells) pass to the Duchy of Benevento's shape in 970 and back in 990. The Otto I page says the Diploma Ottonianum of 962 gave the Pope 'the Exarchate of Ravenna and the Duchy of Spoleto' and that Pandolf of Benevento accepted Otto as overlord from February 967; it does not say who held Spoleto. Benevento's overlordship (967, 972) is not drawn as a vassal tint because no page ends it (the validator needs a paired end).
- Austria: 36 cells drop in 1003 and 17-19 return in 1010 and 1028; no page. The 1177 and 1188 drops (the Baltic coast to Denmark, 46 cells of eastern France to France and Arles) have no page for those years; the Baltic coast is covered by Pomerania's dates (1164, 1181, 1185) only.
- Mecklenburg: the Duchy of Pomerania page says Circipania 'was already lost to Mecklenburg' before 1236, and the Henry the Lion page has nothing on Niklot, 1160 or the Obotrite submission; Mecklenburg's status 1160-1236 rests on Cliopatria's cells.
- Meissen and Lusatia 1018-1033: the Henry II page ('Poland kept Lusatia and Meissen ... nominal terms of vassalage') and the Conrad II page (Mieszko 'invaded Lusatia' in 1028; the Treaty of Merseburg 'required the return of Meissen and Lusatia', dated 1031 for the surrender and July 1033 for the assembly) are not fully consistent; the ledger follows both (vassal 1018-1033, contest 1028-1031).
- Frederick II's 1236 ban on the Duke of Austria and the Austrian and Styrian acquisition: the page has them undated; no event. The Golden Bull of Eger (1213/1214) is not on the Frederick II or Valdemar II pages; the Valdemar II page has an undated recognition of Danish rule 'Two years later' than 1216, which is not recorded. The Lombard communes, the Treaty of Constance and the Third Crusade are not on the pages; the Lombard League enters only as a war with no zone.
- Basel 1006 and the Burgundian succession pact of 1016-1018 are 'not on page' (Henry II); Kingdom of Arles dossier has Basel.
- Rulers: no ruler list was opened (the Holy Roman Empire page has none); the key is omitted rather than filled from memory.
- Area: the infobox gives 1,100,000 km2 for 1150 only; the 1147 and 1139 shapes are 873,727 and 891,038 km2 (ratio 0.79 and 0.81), within a factor of two.

COUNTERPARTS WITHOUT DOSSIERS: the Lutici (Liutizian federation, 983-c.1125; the Elbe-Oder Slavs), Arduin of Ivrea (a one-person rebellion, 1002-1015, not a state), the Lombard League (1167-1250s). The Obotrites have a dossier (eu-07); Pomerania, Kingdom of Bohemia, Kingdom of Poland, Duchy of Benevento, County of Blois, Republic of Pisa, Republic of Genoa, Kingdom of Sicily, Kingdom of Denmark, Kingdom of Arles, Kingdom of France are other groups' rows.

REGION NAMES THE GAZETTEER LACKS: place 'Burg Stargard' (the Stargard Land near Neubrandenburg, used for the 1236 gain).

TOOLING NOTE: events use region diffs of Cliopatria shapes of this row ({'minus': [HRE year a, HRE year b]}) to name exactly the cells that move; each carries a 'text' with the page's words, and the page's own land is named in the note.
